title: P300 dataset BI2014a from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: EEG recordings from 64 participants playing Brain Invaders, a visual P300 brain-computer interface game based on the oddball paradigm. Sixteen dry electrodes recorded responses to flashes of a 36-symbol grid (1 target, 35 non-target). The study examined the feasibility of a calibration-less P300 BCI with dry electrodes. It was conducted at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2014.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 512 Hz from 16 dry gold-alloy electrodes (g.tec g.Sahara cap, g.USBamp amplifier) with the reference on the right earlobe and the ground at FZ. Stimulation used the OpenViBE-based Brain Invaders game, with 12 flash groups per repetition (2 target, 10 non-target). Each session had nine levels, with up to eight attempts per level. A real-time adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean classifier assessed the participants' commands without calibration.
